questions.stem: Pichwai paintings, created on cloth and traditionally hung behind the idol in the Nathdwara temple complex of Rajasthan, primarily depict which deity?

options.option_text: Lord Shiva performing the Tandava cosmic dance
Lord Shrinathji, a form of Lord Krishna
Goddess Durga slaying the demon Mahishasura
Lord Ganesha with his consort Riddhi-Siddhi

questions.explanation: Pichwai ('pich' = back, 'wai' = hanging) are large devotional paintings produced exclusively for the Shrinathji (a child form of Krishna) temple at Nathdwara, depicting Krishna in seasonal and festival contexts. They are a Vaishnava tradition with no connection to Shaiva or Shakta iconography, making Shiva, Durga, and Ganesha incorrect. Candidates sometimes confuse Pichwai with Tanjore painting which also uses temple iconography but covers multiple deities.

questions.stem: UNESCO inscribed the Chhau dance in 2010 on the Intangible Cultural Heritage list. Which of the following is NOT one of the three officially recognized regional styles of Chhau?

options.option_text: Seraikella Chhau, practised in Jharkhand state
Bastar Chhau, practised in Chhattisgarh state
Mayurbhanj Chhau, practised in Odisha state
Purulia Chhau, practised in West Bengal state

questions.explanation: The three UNESCO-recognised Chhau styles are Seraikella (Jharkhand), Mayurbhanj (Odisha), and Purulia (West Bengal). 'Bastar Chhau' does not exist as a recognised school. Candidates often assume Bastar (Chhattisgarh) has a Chhau tradition because it is a famous tribal arts hub (known for Bastar Dhokra metalcraft and Gond painting), but Chhau is geographically absent from Chhattisgarh.

questions.stem: The 'Aipan' art form — geometric and floral patterns drawn using white rice paste on a red-ochre (geru) base — is a ritual folk tradition belonging to which Indian state?

options.option_text: Himachal Pradesh (Kinnaur tribal region)
Uttarakhand (Kumaon hill folk tradition)
Jammu & Kashmir (Dogra cultural belt)
Sikkim (Lepcha indigenous community)

questions.explanation: Aipan is the traditional threshold/floor art of the Kumaon region of Uttarakhand, made by women during festivals such as Navratri and Janmashtami. It received a Geographical Indication (GI) tag in 2021. Himachal Pradesh is a common distractor because it shares a Himalayan cultural zone with Uttarakhand and is known for Chamba Rumal embroidery and Kangra miniatures — but Aipan is specifically Kumaoni.

questions.stem: The 'Urumi' — a coiled, whip-like sword made of spring steel that can be worn around the waist — is a signature advanced weapon of which Indian martial art?

options.option_text: Gatka, the traditional Sikh martial art of Punjab
Kalaripayattu, the ancient martial art of Kerala
Silambam, the staff-based martial art of Tamil Nadu
Thang-ta, the armed martial tradition of Manipur

questions.explanation: The Urumi (also called Chuttuval, meaning 'coiling sword') is exclusive to Kalaripayattu and is taught only to advanced practitioners because its flexible blade is dangerous without mastery. Silambam exclusively uses a bamboo staff; Gatka uses kirpan, chakkar, and stick forms; Thang-ta uses the thang (sword) and ta (spear). Silambam is the most tempting distractor as it also originates in South India, but it has no sword tradition.

questions.stem: Kalighat paintings, produced by scroll-painter communities (patuas) near the Kalighat Kali temple in Kolkata during the 19th century, are visually distinguished by which characteristic style?

options.option_text: Intricate gold leaf borders and geometric floral patterns
Bold flowing outlines, flat colours, and simplified forms
Detailed landscape backgrounds with architectural motifs
Minute stippling technique with layered translucent washes

questions.explanation: Kalighat's hallmark is its radical simplification: a few bold, sweeping brushstrokes define the figure against a plain background, with flat colour fills and no decorative border work. This directness influenced Jamini Roy and later modernists. Gold leaf and geometric borders are features of Tanjore painting, while stippling and layered washes describe Mughal/Rajput miniature technique — both are incorrect here.

questions.stem: The Basohli school of Pahari painting (flourished c. 1660–1730, Jammu region) employed a unique material innovation: actual iridescent elytra (wing cases of the jewel beetle) were embedded in the painting to depict which element?

options.option_text: Shimmering water bodies and sacred river currents
Emerald jewellery and gem-studded ornaments worn by figures
Lush forest canopies and tree foliage in landscapes
Night-sky stars and constellations in celestial compositions

questions.explanation: Basohli painters embedded the iridescent green wing cases of the jewel beetle (Sternocera species) into the painted surface to simulate the sheen of real emeralds in necklaces, waistbands, and crowns — a diagnostic feature that distinguishes Basohli from all later Pahari sub-schools (Guler, Kangra, Chamba). The most tempting distractor is water bodies, since the beetle-wing green is aquamarine, but the convention is specifically for gem ornaments, as confirmed by comparative Basohli-Mughal scholarship.

questions.stem: 'Huyen Langlon' is the comprehensive indigenous martial system of Manipur. Which of the following correctly pairs its two constituent disciplines?

options.option_text: Mukna (traditional wrestling) and Yubi Lakpi (polo variant)
Thang-ta (armed combat) and Sarit Sarak (unarmed combat)
Pari-khanda (sword and shield) and Mallakhamb (pole gymnastics)
Lathi Khela (staff combat) and Mardaani Khel (sword techniques)

questions.explanation: Huyen Langlon ('art of the sword and spear') comprises Thang-ta (thang = sword, ta = spear; weapon-based combat) and Sarit Sarak (unarmed grappling and striking). Mukna is a separate Manipuri traditional wrestling sport, and Yubi Lakpi is a traditional Manipuri coconut polo game — both are Manipuri but are not parts of Huyen Langlon. Pari-khanda belongs to Bihar/Rajasthan and Mardaani Khel to Maharashtra, making Option D a geography-error trap targeting candidates who confuse regional martial arts.
